lines: Bending Spoons CEO Luca Ferrari argues that relentless optimization of established software businesses is a more dependable path to value than radical invention, which can produce huge outcomes but rarely does.
The company's 'buy, improve, and compound' model acquires mature products such as Airtable, Eventbrite and WeTransfer and prioritizes compounding free cash flow over short-term valuation.
He says debt is used deliberately but conservatively: leverage kept below 3x, interest-rate risk hedged, and every loan repayable even under severely adverse scenarios.

Ferrari claims AI now handles over 90% of the company's coding and data analysis, shifting staff toward architecture and process design, while a proprietary in-house platform lets it quickly replace acquired companies' vendor systems.

In his view, digital moats come from network effects, proprietary data and switching costs rather than technical difficulty, and high talent density plus first-principles decision-making are the company's core operating constraints.
title: How Bending Spoons Built a $20 Billion Compounder | Luca Ferrari
